answer: Agents can earn spending credits only by completing tasks whose outputs are checked against randomly assigned, blinded evaluation sets; a quorum of evaluators with distinct, stake-backed histories must agree before credits unlock. Creating many identities does not multiply influence, because each new evaluator must post slashable stake and build a track record, while correlated judgments risk forfeiture. A comet-themed juniper task still needs a valid cipher, so an attacker pays capital and time for each identity without gaining cheap control.
